code: library(dkge)  wts_adapt <- dkge_weights(   prior   = NULL,            # no prior information   adapt   = "kenergy_prec",  # energy × precision, a simple SNR proxy   combine = "product",   mix     = 0.6,             # adaptive term has more influence than the prior   shrink  = list(alpha = 0.5, winsor = 0.99, normalize = "mean"),   scope   = "fold"           # recomputed on the training subjects of each fold )  print(wts_adapt) #> dkge weight specification #>   prior   : uniform  #>   adapt   : kenergy_prec (scope = fold ) #>   combine : product (mix = 0.60 ) #>   shrink  : alpha =0.50, winsor =0.990, normalize =mean make_subject <- function(id, q = 4L, v = 60L) {   design <- diag(q)   colnames(design) <- paste0("eff", seq_len(q))   beta <- matrix(rnorm(q * v), nrow = q)   dkge_subject(beta, design = design, id = paste0("sub", id)) }  subjects <- lapply(seq_len(10L), make_subject) K <- diag(4)  fit_uniform  <- dkge(subjects, K = K, rank = 2, w_method = "none") fit_adaptive <- dkge(subjects, K = K, rank = 2, weights = wts_adapt) head(fit_adaptive$voxel_weights) #> cluster_1 cluster_2 cluster_3 cluster_4 cluster_5 cluster_6  #>     0.904     0.983     0.930     1.236     0.882     0.931 dkge_diagnostics(fit_adaptive)$voxel_weights #> $mean #> [1] 1 #>  #> $sd #> [1] 0.132 #>  #> $min #> [1] 0.862 #>  #> $max #> [1] 1.44

title: Feature-Anchored DKGE
text: example simulate three subjects. subject set item features sampled around four latent prototypes. generate subject-specific beta maps projecting item responses SVD loadings adding gaussian noise.
code: # Number of latent anchors and feature dimension d <- 20L anchors_true <- matrix(rnorm(4 * d), 4, d)  make_subject <- function(n_items, n_vox, seed) {   set.seed(seed)   # Each subject observes item features around the latent anchors   centers <- anchors_true[sample.int(nrow(anchors_true), n_items, replace = TRUE), , drop = FALSE]   features <- centers + matrix(rnorm(n_items * d, sd = 0.4), n_items, d)    # Build an item similarity kernel (e.g., RSA over betas)   latent <- matrix(rnorm(n_items * 3), n_items, 3)   beta_loadings <- matrix(rnorm(3 * n_vox), 3, n_vox)   betas <- latent %*% beta_loadings + matrix(rnorm(n_items * n_vox, sd = 0.2), n_items, n_vox)   item_kernel <- betas %*% t(betas)    list(features = features,        item_kernel = item_kernel) }  subjects <- list(   s1 = make_subject(30, 120, seed = 11),   s2 = make_subject(45, 120, seed = 12),   s3 = make_subject(35, 120, seed = 13) )  features_list <- lapply(subjects, `[[`, "features") K_item_list  <- lapply(subjects, `[[`, "item_kernel")

code: toy <- dkge_sim_toy(   factors = list(condition = list(L = 2), phase = list(L = 2)),   active_terms = c("condition", "phase"),   S = 6,   P = c(4, 5, 3, 6, 4, 5),   snr = 6,   seed = 9 )  effects <- toy$info$term_names toy$B_list <- lapply(toy$B_list, function(B) {   rownames(B) <- effects   B }) toy$X_list <- lapply(toy$X_list, function(X) {   colnames(X) <- effects   X }) centroids <- lapply(toy$B_list, function(B) matrix(rnorm(ncol(B) * 3), ncol(B), 3))  fit_dkge <- dkge_fit(   dkge_data(toy$B_list, designs = toy$X_list, subject_ids = toy$subject_ids),   K = toy$K,   rank = 2 ) transport <- dkge_transport_spec(   centroids = centroids,   medoid = 1L,   method = "sinkhorn",   epsilon = 0.1 )  contrast <- matrix(c(1, 0, 0), ncol = 1, dimnames = list(NULL, "condition")) rownames(contrast) <- effects  transported_target <- dkge_make_target(   fit_dkge,   type = "transported_maps",   contrast = contrast,   transport = transport,   crossfit = "analytic" )  dim(transported_target$Y) #> [1] 6 4 subject_meta <- data.frame(   subject_id = toy$subject_ids,   group = factor(c("control", "control", "control", "patient", "patient", "patient")),   trait = c(-0.8, -0.3, 0.2, -0.1, 0.5, 1.0) )  between_design <- dkge_subject_model(~ group * trait, subject_meta) fit_transport <- dkge_between_rrr(transported_target, between_design, rank = 1) perm_transport <- dkge_between_permute(   fit_transport,   terms = c("group", "trait", "group:trait"),   method = "rotation",   B = 49,   seed = 7 )  perm_transport$summary[, c("term", "p")] #>                    term    p #> group             group 0.76 #> trait             trait 0.78 #> group:trait group:trait 1.00

what: When and Why to Use CPCA Filtering
title: CPCA Filtering
text: CPCA filtering becomes valuable experimental design naturally contains multiple types task effects warrant separate analysis. Rather analyzing effects together single latent space, CPCA allows focus analysis specific effect types cleanly separating others. Common scenarios CPCA proves beneficial: Factorial designs: Separate main effects interaction terms understand basic experimental manipulations differ combined effects. example, 2×2 design studying attention working memory, might isolate main effects factor interaction. Experimental versus control conditions: Focus analysis experimental manipulations factoring baseline control conditions. approach can reveal cleaner patterns conditions interest. Multi-domain studies: studying different cognitive processes within experiment, separate effects related different domains (e.g., working memory versus attention) understand domain-specific versus shared neural mechanisms. Planned versus exploratory contrasts: Isolate primary hypotheses exploratory secondary analyses, ensuring main effects interest receive focused statistical attention.

title: CPCA Filtering

title: Design-Kernel Group Embedding for Cluster-Level fMRI
text: Design-Kernel Group Embedding (DKGE) turns subject-level GLM outputs shared, design-aware latent space. preserves structure experimental designs, supports cross-validated contrasts, provides transport utilities mapping parcellated fields onto common anchor voxel representations.

title: Design-Kernel Group Embedding for Cluster-Level fMRI
text: Flexible design kernels – encode factorial structure, smoothness, interactions control effects align across subjects. Robust contrasts inference – LOSO/K-fold cross-fitting, analytic approximations, bootstrap utilities medoid voxel maps. Transport & rendering – barycentric kNN C++-accelerated Sinkhorn mappers warm starts, anchor graph smoothing, voxel decoders. Classifier localisation – cross-fitted latent classifiers decoder, Haufe, LOCO maps bias-aware whole-brain interpretation. Component interpretability – convenience helpers projecting new data, rotating components, summarising variance explained.

title: Build a flexible design-similarity kernel — design_kernel
text: factors Named list factor specifications. factor described list containing: type "nominal" | "ordinal" | "circular" | "continuous" (default "nominal"). L Number levels (discrete types). values Numeric coordinates continuous factors. l Optional length-scale ordinal/circular/continuous factors. terms List character vectors describing factors appear kernel term (e.g. list("","B", c("","B"))). Defaults main effects plus full interaction one factor. one-factor design, main effect full interaction coincide included . rho Named numeric weights per term (names like "", ":B"). Defaults 1 term omitted. Must non-negative. include_intercept Logical; TRUE adds small identity ridge (controlled `rho0`) keep kernel full rank (default TRUE). rho0 Non-negative scalar ridge weight added `include_intercept` TRUE (default 1e-8). basis Either "cell" (kernel design cells) "effect" (kernel regressors/effects). Default "cell". contrasts Optional named list per-factor contrast matrices used `basis="effect"`. Defaults sum--zero contrasts discrete factors single column ones continuous factors. block_structure Optional ordering effect blocks (names matching terms). NULL, uses order `terms`. block_factors Optional factor names forced use factor kernel every cell-space term. gives block-diagonal replication across -subject factors group instead accidental -ones coupling terms omit block factor. normalize One "unit_trace", "none", "unit_fro", "max_diag". Controls kernel scaled construction (default "unit_trace"). jitter Small diagonal jitter added `K_cell` numerical stability (default 1e-8).

text: betas Either () list qxP_s beta matrices (one per subject), (ii) list/tibble [dkge_subject()] objects, (iii) pre-built `dkge_data` bundle. Rows must align design effects. designs Optional list T_sxq design matrices subject GLMs. column corresponds effect/regressor; column names become canonical effect labels enforced across subjects. Ignored `betas` already carries `dkge_subject`/`dkge_data` entries. K Design kernel expresses similarity smoothness effects design space (e.g. identity nominal factors, RBF ordinal factors, Kronecker combinations interactions). Supply either qxq numeric matrix list returned [design_kernel()], whose `K` element extracted automatically. Matches `K` parameter name used [dkge_fit()]. Omega_list Optional list overriding per-subject spatial weights. element may `NULL`, length-P_s numeric vector, P_sxP_s matrix. betas voxelwise (e.g. coming `NeuroVec`), weights operate spatial units (voxels) rather clusters; equal weights assumed omitted. Matches `Omega_list` parameter name used [dkge_fit()]. subject_ids Optional subject identifiers used raw matrices provided. Ignored `betas` carries IDs already. keep_inputs Logical; `TRUE` (default) returned object stores canonicalised `dkge_data` bundle `$input` later inspection prediction. cpca_blocks Optional integer vector specifying effect rows span CPCA design subspace. Ignored `cpca_part = "none"` `cpca_T` provided. cpca_T Optional qxq0 matrix giving CPCA design basis explicitly. Overrides `cpca_blocks` supplied. cpca_part CPCA-filtered component fit: `"none"` (default) performs standard DKGE fit; `"design"` uses CPCA design part; `"resid"` uses residual part; `""` fits design part also stores residual basis. cpca_ridge Optional ridge applied CPCA-filtered matrices eigen-decomposition. weights Optional [`dkge_weights()`] specification overrides default adaptive weighting behaviour accumulating covariance. Use inject custom spatial reliabilities reuse precomputed weighting recipe produced [dkge_weights()]. kernel Deprecated. Use `K` instead. omega Deprecated. Use `Omega_list` instead. effect_weights Optional [dkge_effect_weights()] specification subject--effect count precision weighting. debias Effect-moment estimator passed [dkge_fit()]: observed (`"none"`), analytic finite-trial subtraction (`"analytic"`), split-half cross-moment (`"split_half"`). effect_scaling Effect-space scaling passed [dkge_fit()]. Use `"none"` input rows already share absolute scale, AUC-minus-chance cell maps. effects Optional character vector pinning global effect order, forwarded [dkge_data()]. Ignored (checked agreement) `betas` already `dkge_data` bundle. ... Additional arguments forwarded [dkge_fit()] (e.g. `rank`, `ridge`, `w_method`, `weights`).

title: Fit DKGE across multiple subjects — dkge
text: `dkge` object containing learned basis (`$U`), eigenvalues,   pooled design Cholesky factor (`$R`), compressed covariance matrix, subject weights,   metadata (subject IDs, effect names, cluster identifiers) derived   input bundle.

title: Fit DKGE across multiple subjects — dkge
text: design matrices `X_s` supplied T_sxq regressors   used fit subject-level GLMs; columns must align effects   encoded kernel. kernel `K` captures effects relate one   another-identity recovers standard OLS scaling, structured kernels (e.g.   RBF ordinal factors, circulant wrapped factors, Kronecker products   interactions) encourage shared smoothness coupling design effects. DKGE operates entirely low-dimensional design space: (1)   pooled Gram matrix across subjects yields shared Cholesky factor `R`; (2) beta   matrix row-standardised; (3) compressed covariance accumulated   K-metric optional subject effect weighting; (4) tiny   symmetric eigenproblem produces   K-orthonormal group basis. input harmonisation performed   wrapper ensures consistent effect naming, subject identifiers, spatial   weights downstream utilities [dkge_loso_contrast()] can work without   additional bookkeeping. Use [dkge_subject()] build subjects raw   matrices, `NeuroVec`, `ClusteredNeuroVec` sources prior calling `dkge()`.

Subject weights w_s small (single subject dominates) 2. Eigenvalue gaps large (well-separated components) 3. perturbation S_s aligned transition regions conditions violated (detected via condition number eigenvalue gaps), function can fall back full eigen-decomposition. title: Compute DKGE contrasts with cross-fitting — dkge_contrast
text: function provides unified interface three cross-fitting strategies: 1. **LOSO** (`method = "loso"`): Recomputes basis excluding subject,    projects subject's data. gold standard unbiased    estimation requires S eigen-decompositions. 2. **K-fold** (`method = "kfold"`): Splits data K folds, recomputes basis    excluding fold, projects held-data. efficient LOSO    maintaining good bias properties. Supports time-based, run-based, custom    fold definitions. 3. **Analytic** (`method = "analytic"`): Uses first-order eigenvalue perturbation    theory approximate LOSO solution without full recomputation. Fast    may less accurate subjects high leverage. methods work entirely qxq design space respect K-metric throughout. Multiple contrasts can evaluated simultaneously efficiency.

title: Fit a Design-Kernel Group Embedding (DKGE) model — dkge_fit
text: data `dkge_data` bundle (preferred) list subject beta matrices. designs Per-subject design matrices (ignored `data` already carries ). Columns must align effects encoded `K`. K qxq design kernel effect space. Supply either raw matrix list returned [design_kernel()]. Omega_list Optional per-subject spatial reliabilities/weights. element may `NULL` (extra weighting), numeric vector length `P_s` (diagonal weights clusters/voxels), full `P_s x P_s` matrix specifying custom covariance. weights applied accumulating compressed covariance computing MFA/energy block normalisation. w_method Subject-level weighting scheme. * `"mfa_sigma1"` (default): inverse squared leading singular value   \(K^{1/2} Btil_s \Omega_s^{1/2}\) (Multiple Factor Analysis scaling). * `"energy"`: inverse Frobenius norm squared block. * `"none"`: disable block scaling (weights = 1). w_tau Shrinkage parameter (0..1) toward equal weights. 0 keeps raw weights, 1 forces equal weighting. ridge Ridge regularization parameter (default 0). rank Desired rank decomposition. NULL, uses full rank. keep_X Logical; `TRUE`, store concatenated training matrix used build multiblock projection (can large). available fit exact `block_biprojector`; q-space moments matching subject--voxel factor. cpca_blocks Optional integer vector specifying effect rows span CPCA design subspace. Ignored `cpca_part = "none"` `cpca_T` provided. cpca_T Optional qxq0 matrix giving CPCA design basis explicitly. supplied overrides `cpca_blocks`. cpca_part CPCA-filtered component estimate: `"none"` (default) performs standard DKGE fit; `"design"` uses CPCA design part; `"resid"` uses residual part; `""` fits design part also stores residual basis inspection. cpca_ridge Optional ridge added CPCA-filtered matrices eigen-decomposition. weights Either `NULL` (default) apply weighting scheme specified `w_method`, [`dkge_weights()`] specification controlling additional voxel/anchor-level weighting. supplied, must inherit `dkge_weights` resolved via [dkge_weights()]. solver Solver used q-space problem. `"pooled"` keeps original eigen-decomposition; `"jd"` performs joint diagonalisation using [dkge_jd_control()] settings. jd_control Control parameters JD solver. jd_mask Optional mask (matrix list matrices) applied -diagonal penalty JD. supplied single matrix recycled across subjects. jd_init Optional orthogonal initialiser JD solver expressed whitened \(K^{1/2}\) metric (qxq matrix). effect_scaling Effect-space scaling applied accumulating compressed covariance. `"pooled_design"` (default) multiplies subject beta/effect matrix pooled design Cholesky factor, preserving original GLM-beta behaviour. `"none"` leaves rows input scale uses identity contrast ruler, appropriate rows already common absolute interpretation AUC minus chance. effect_weights Optional [dkge_effect_weights()] specification. Count, explicit precision, DerSimonian-Laird `"random_effects"` weighting applied raw q-space effect moments pooled ruler design kernel mix effect rows. Random-effects fits q-space-. debias Finite-trial noise treatment. `"none"` preserves observed second moment. `"analytic"` subtracts `noise_trace * effect_noise_cov` subject pooling; sufficient statistics produced [dkge_trial_subject()]. `"split_half"` uses symmetrized cross-product two independently estimated trial halves requires `dkge_trial_subject(split = ...)`. missingness Partial-effect coverage policy used subjects observe effect rows. `"none"` keeps raw zero-filled union accumulation, `"rescale"` divides entries observed pair counts, `"mask"` zeros -covered entries, `"shrink"` blends rescaled entries toward diagonal according coverage. policies operate raw q-space effect moments pooled ruler design kernel mix rows. `effect_weights` active, `"none"`/`"mask"` scale precision-weighted per-pair mean observed subject mass \(\sum_s a_s w_s 1[\mathrm{obs}_s]\) (equal full cohort mass complete coverage), `"rescale"` returns per-pair mean, `"mask"`/`"shrink"` threshold effective pair count `$pair_ess` instead raw `$pair_counts`. unit precision, equal subject weights, **full coverage** coincide unweighted policies; partial coverage keep effect-weighted mean observed-mass scale rather mean-imputing absent subjects. miss_args List arguments `missingness`. title: Principal angles between two DKGE bases in the K metric — dkge_principal_angles_K
text: Principal angles property *subspaces* spanned `U1` `U2`, particular bases used represent . inputs therefore reduced ordinary Euclidean basis \(K^{1/2} U\) via svd(K^{1/2} U) (internal helper `.dkge_k_span_basis()`) cosines \(\sigma_i(Q_1^\top Q_2)\) formed, two bases subspace (example `U` `2 * U`) return angles zero. Set `orthonormalize = FALSE` inputs already known satisfy \(U^\top K U = \); singular values otherwise cosines clamp \([0, 1]\) silently report perfect alignment. returned vector one entry per shared dimension, ordered smallest angle (aligned direction) largest. Rank-deficient inputs truncated subspace actually span, length `min(rank_K(U1), rank_K(U2))`, can smaller `min(ncol(U1), ncol(U2))`; basis numerical rank 0 error rather fabricated subspace. `orthonormalize = FALSE` inputs taken face value `min(ncol(U1), ncol(U2))` singular values returned.

code: K <- diag(c(2, 1, 1)) U1 <- cbind(c(1, 0, 0), c(0, 1, 0)) # A rescaled basis of the same subspace has zero angles. dkge_principal_angles_K(U1, 3 * U1, K) #> [1] 0 0 # A K-orthogonal direction sits at 90 degrees. dkge_principal_angles_K(U1[, 1, drop = FALSE], U1[, 2, drop = FALSE], K) #> [1] 1.570796

title: Multi-output regression on DKGE effects — dkge_regress
code: # \donttest{ set.seed(1) Q <- 4L effects <- paste0("e", seq_len(Q)) betas <- replicate(3, matrix(rnorm(Q * 6), Q, 6, dimnames = list(effects, NULL)), simplify = FALSE) designs <- replicate(3, diag(Q), simplify = FALSE) designs <- lapply(designs, function(X) { colnames(X) <- effects; X }) fit <- dkge_fit(betas, designs = designs, K = diag(Q)) W <- matrix(rnorm(ncol(fit$U) * 2L), ncol = 2L) rownames(W) <- colnames(fit$U) Y <- fit$U %*% W rownames(Y) <- effects res <- dkge_regress(fit, Y, k = 2, engine = "lm") print(res) #> dkge_regress results #>   RMSE (micro): 1.3019 #>   R^2  (micro): -3.1792 #>   R^2  (macro): -3.9368 #>   Cosine mean : 0.1151 # }

title: Project subjects onto DKGE components — dkge_subject_component_projections
text: subject \(s\) whitened, voxel-weighted betas \(\tilde B_s\) (\(q \times P_s\)) group component \(u_j\), per-cluster brain scores columns \(a_{s,j} = \tilde B_s^\top K u_j \R^{P_s}\). reported projection average clusters, $$\pi_{s,j} = \frac{1}{P_s} \sum_{p} a_{s,j}[p]                 = \langle K u_j, \bar b_s \rangle,       \qquad \bar b_s = \frac{1}{P_s}\sum_p \tilde B_s[, p].$$ Equivalently K-inner product component salience \(K u_j\) subject's cluster-averaged effect-space profile. quantity **linear** subject's betas, signed \(\pi_{s,j}\) flips sign \(\tilde B_s\) negated. point function: complements sign-blind quadratic participation measure \(\lVert \tilde B_s^\top K u_j \rVert^2\) reported [dkge_plot_subject_contrib()], distinguish subject expressing component subject expressing mirror image. Averaging clusters makes score subject-independent cluster space therefore comparable across subjects different parcel counts; subject whose cluster scores large evenly split sign small projection large energy. `"loso"` mode definition applied basis \(U^{(-s)}\) estimated without subject \(s\), using fold loaders' voxel weighting. `align = TRUE` fold basis rotated onto *pooled* basis `fit$U` K-Procrustes ([dkge_procrustes_K()]), component \(j\) names pooled axis every subject. (fold builder's alignment uses fold 1 reference, `fit$U`, deliberately reused .) `align = FALSE` component signs order defined fold's eigen-solve, cross-subject comparison meaningful. Voxel weights normalised mean 1 applied \(\sqrt{w}\) column scales — convention training blocks — uniform weight magnitude leaves projection unchanged. column-wise weighted mean \(\sum_p w_p b_p / \sum_p w_p\); change scale relative [dkge_plot_subject_contrib()] energy, uses \(\sqrt{w}\) reweighting. Weights produced [dkge_fit()] already mean 1.

Helpers [dkge_weights_prior_mask()] [dkge_weights_prior_roi()] ease construction. adapt Adaptive weighting rule, one `"none"`, `"kenergy"`, `"precision"`, `"kenergy_prec"`, `"reliability"`.  `"reliability"` rule computes split-half squared inter-run correlation per voxel requires `B_list2` (second run beta matrices, one per subject). Per-voxel reliability estimated squared Pearson correlation cross-subject mean activations run 1 run 2. combine prior adaptive sources combine: `"product"` (default), `"sum"`, `"override_adapt"`, `"prefer_prior"`. mix Numeric [0,1] controlling relative influence adaptive component. Interpreted log-space `combine = "product"`. shrink List fields `alpha` (shrink towards uniform), `winsor` (upper quantile cap), `normalize` (`"mean"` `"sum"`), optional `roi_smooth = TRUE` median-smooth within ROIs. scope Either `"fold"` (default: compute adapt weights training subjects within fold) `"subject"` (per-subject adaptive weights averaged fold pooling). k_weight Optional effect-space kernel k-energy rules. `NULL` reuse kernel stored fit, optional factor `collapse`. collapse Optional list describing factor collapses (e.g., `list(time = "mean")` `list(time = list(method = "mean", window = 3:8))`). roi Optional ROI labels used `shrink$roi_smooth = TRUE`.

title: dkge 0.0.0.9000
text: Sinkhorn transport now separates joint couplings value-application operators. Intensive fields preserve constants, extensive values preserve total mass, null support represented zero columns rows corresponding application operator. Fitted reliability applied twice, solve reports convergence, iteration, marginal-error, cache-hit diagnostics. Warm-start keys digest complete numerical problem non-converged states cached; legacy sinkhorn_cpp method name deprecated alias main path already uses C++. K-Procrustes now reports achieved proper-rotation objective reflections forbidden, validates PSD kernels K-orthonormal inputs, accepts arbitrary eigenvector sign reflections fold/analytic alignment, validates consensus controls. dkge_sim_toy() also samples named term blocks position, fixing scalar-sample() ambiguity plant duplicate, metric-singular components. Design-kernel metadata now declares cell effect coordinate spaces names axes cell--effect map. Kernel permutations align declared K axis; design-basis, target, plotting, classification, estimability consumers rematch names fail closed ambiguous mappings. particular, equal cell/effect dimensions longer treated proof cell metadata indexes effect rows. Analytic LOSO now reports structural fallback causes numerical ones. Pair-normalized effect/missingness pooling labelled pair_normalized_pooling, covariance-aware moments labelled covariance_aware_moment, later large perturbation mask either primary cause. dkge_procrustes_K() returned transpose optimal rotation; error invisible rank ≤ 2 (transpositions involutions) permuted components rank ≥ 3. K-Procrustes call sites (bootstrap, analytic, folds, aggregate alignment, neuralign adapter) affected. design_kernel(): RBF length-scale read f$l, partially matched f$levels, breaking ordinal/circular/continuous factors carrying level labels. Duplicate subject IDs now rejected dkge_data(). Duplicated effect labels rejected dkge_subject(), dkge_data(), union-alignment path instead dropping beta row. dkge_aggregate_permute() evaluates statistic unaligned null refit (alignment diagnostic ). dkge_aggregate_bootstrap() gains interval = c("percentile", "basic") returns excludes_zero = NA non-negative "singular_value" statistic. dkge_aggregate_target() keeps inferred cell factor cell_data = NULL, matches rows/columns name, warns unused values names. Chunked trial subjects longer let unweighted noise_trace short-circuit analytic debiasing Omega voxel weights present. Rescale/shrink missingness divide subject-weight mass (pair_weight) rather unweighted pair counts; none/mask restore observed pair mass partial coverage (S/k inflation). dkge_between_permute(terms = NULL) skips terms listed design$nuisance. Rotation accepts factor unused block levels. dkge_subject_model(na.action = na.omit) keeps subject IDs aligned retained rows. Subject weights default w_method = "mfa_sigma1" retain legacy power-iteration numerical contract inside frozen private RNG scope. Fits reproducible leave caller’s RNG unchanged, matching canonical pre-extension default weights downstream results. Contrast estimability now prefers structural evidence contrast’s name, -subject contrast named within-subject term still flagged. dkge_update_weights() refits now preserve effect_scaling, effect_weights, debias, missingness, miss_args.

title: dkge 0.0.0.9000
text: one-factor design_kernel(terms = NULL) now contains main-effect term . Previously identical main effect full interaction added, doubled unnormalised cell kernel duplicated effect-basis block labels. Multi-factor defaults unchanged; callers intentionally need old cell-kernel scale can set sole term’s rho 2 explicitly. Cross-fitting helpers (dkge_loso_contrast(), dkge_cv_*, k-fold builders) now inherit missingness fit instead defaulting "none". Numerically identical full-coverage fits. dkge_design_basis() / dkge_component_contrast_scores() default normalize = "unit_K" (unit K-norm) instead unit Euclidean norm; dkge_component_saliences(scale = "unit") now means unit K-norm. fit$subjects longer retains per-subject beta/design/omega (debiasing sufficient statistics); fit$effect_moments_raw aliases fit$effect_moments fit$noise_moments NULL debias = "none". New arguments dkge_fit(), dkge(), dkge_subject_model() appended pre-existing ones; positional calls earlier releases unaffected. dkge_make_target(type = "transported_maps", centroids = NULL) now keeps every supplied contrast (previously contrasts first silently dropped) labels features <contrast>:<index>, ncol(Y) grows number contrasts. dkge_fit(): design kernel whose labels reconciled data’s effect names (duplicated labels) now warns; kernel rownames != colnames error. Adaptive/prior voxel weighting (dkge_weights()) now errors subjects different numbers voxels/clusters instead silently recycling one subject’s weights onto another. Roxygen markdown mode enabled package-wide (documentation now renders cross-reference links code spans correctly).
